newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on inflows.

text.p: * Volume thins to $151.10 million from $212.50 million
Dollar inflows buoyed the Philippine peso at the close on Monday to 26.281 from 26.285, traders said.

Banks were also selling their dollars in exchange for pesos to generate more liquidity in view of the high demand for pesos to correct their four-day reserve positions during the weekend, which included a holiday, traders said.
As expected, the Central Bank intervened in the market.
"The Central Bank was a net buyer today," said a dealer.
Traders said they saw the Central Bank buying dollars at 26.282 pesos for same-day delivery in view of the inflows from overseas workers remittances and portfolio investments.
In late trades, however, the Central Bank eventually let go of the market, which pushed the peso to close at its day-high of 26.281 pesos after opening at its low of 26.285.
"The Central Bank may have thought it could buy dollars at lower levels," a dealer said.
The day's average was at 26.283 from 26.282.
